P-creatinin (plasma creatinine) is a laboratory test parameter utilized in the Danish national quality program for atrial fibrillation to assess kidney function. It serves as an alternative laboratory parameter to serum creatinine for evaluating renal function, specifically within the context of safety monitoring for patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) [^src1]. 

Within the clinical quality indicators framework, P-creatinin is the core measurement for [[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]]. This indicator tracks the proportion of atrial fibrillation patients on DOAC therapy who receive at least one annual measurement of their P-creatinin levels [^src1]. Monitoring this parameter is a critical safety requirement, as the safe administration and dosing of DOACs depend on regular assessments of renal function [^src2]. The national tracking of these measurements relies on a complex data infrastructure, utilizing specific NPU codes to collect and analyze laboratory data across different regions and hospital clusters in Denmark [^src2].
